# opencode-plugin-timer

An OpenCode V2 plugin that gives each session a single repeating or one-shot
timer. When the timer fires, it injects a synthetic message containing the
instruction you originally gave it, so the agent does the work again and reports
back.

Built with TypeScript, Node.js APIs, and [`node-cron`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/node-cron).
The public tool surface speaks seconds; node-cron provides the one-second clock.

## Tools

| Tool | Input | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `timer_start` | `message`, `interval_seconds`, optional `once`, `label`, `force` | Starts or replaces the session's single timer. A running timer is rejected unless `force: true`. |
| `timer_status` | none | Shows mode, interval, original message, last tick, next tick, and run count. |
| `timer_stop` | none | Stops and removes the timer, including a completed one-shot record. |

`interval_seconds` is a whole number, minimum `10`, maximum `31_536_000`
(one year). Repeating is the default. `once: true` fires after the delay and
marks the timer completed.

## Behaviour

- **One timer per session.** There is no edit operation. `force: true` stops a
  running timer and starts the new one; without it, starting fails.
- **Session-scoped.** Timers are stored in a `Map` keyed by the session ID from
  the tool call context. A timer created in one session never fires, reports, or
  stops in another. The only shared object is the node-cron clock, and it only
  asks the service which timers are due.
- **Code Mode.** The tools are also exposed to Code Mode, so a script can call
  `tools.timer.start`, `tools.timer.status`, and `tools.timer.stop`.
- **Steer delivery.** Every tick admits a synthetic message with
  `delivery: "steer"` and `resume: true`. It is injected at the next safe step
  boundary — after the current tool call or step — so it interrupts the current
  turn instead of waiting for the whole turn to finish. Steer delivery takes
  priority over queued input at that boundary.
- **Synthetic, not user input.** Each message is typed `synthetic` and carries
  `metadata.source: "timer"`, so it is distinguishable from real user prompts
  and from other plugins' messages.
- **No inbox cancellation.** The plugin API does not expose
  `session.inbox.cancel`. `timer_stop` cancels future ticks, but synthetic
  messages already in the inbox will still be delivered.
- **In-memory.** Plugin reload, server restart, or moving the session clears
  timers. Nothing is written to plugin storage.
- **No missed-tick burst.** If the event loop was blocked or the machine slept,
  a repeating timer fires once and advances to the next future slot. Missed
  slots are not replayed.
- **Session deletion.** If the synthetic admission fails (for example, the
  session was removed), the error is logged and the timer keeps its schedule.
  Use `timer_stop` or let the next tick retry.

## Synthetic message

Repeating timer:

```text
[Timer: watch deploy · tick #3]

Check whether the deploy finished. Report any new errors.

Do that again and report back. If you're comparing over time, save a small snapshot first. The timer repeats automatically — don't create another.
```

One-shot timer:

```text
[Timer: watch deploy · one-shot, completed]

Check whether the deploy finished. Report any new errors.

Complete the task and report back.
```

The original `message` is stored verbatim. It is repeated in every tick because
session compaction may remove the tool call that created the timer.

## Install

Once published:

```sh
opencode plugin add opencode-plugin-timer
```

### Local / global link

```sh
cd /code/opencode-plugin-timer
npm link
```

Add the plugin's source directory to the global config at
`~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc`:

```jsonc
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "plugins": ["/code/opencode-plugin-timer/src"]
}
```

Point at `src` rather than the package root. `Host.resolve` can load
`src/server.ts` directly; the package root relies on a registry self-reference
that is not available for an unpublished, globally linked package. The
published package uses `dist/index.js`.

### Slash command

Create `~/.config/opencode/commands/timer.md`:

```md
---
description: Manage the session timer
agent: build
---

Manage the session timer.

Arguments: $ARGUMENTS

- `timer_start` — start or replace the session timer.
- `timer_status` — show the current timer.
- `timer_stop` — stop and remove the timer.

Call the tool that matches the request. Use `force: true` with `timer_start` to replace a running timer.
```

Then use `/timer 30 check the build`, `/timer status`, or `/timer stop`.

## Development

```sh
npm install
npm run check
npm run build
npm run pack:check
```

`npm test` uses Bun's test runner. The scheduler is a pure due-time service, so
the tests inject a clock and never wait on real timers.

The published package uses built JavaScript from `dist/`, not TypeScript. See
[RELEASING.md](RELEASING.md) for the npm release flow and the `NPM_TOKEN` CI
setup.

## Layout

```text
src/
  clock.ts    node-cron one-second heartbeat
  format.ts   synthetic message, status, and duration text
  index.ts    OpenCode plugin and tool registration
  server.ts   local dev entrypoint
  timer.ts    session-scoped timer state and due-time logic
  types.ts    shared types
test/
  format.test.ts
  timer.test.ts
```
